identity.runtime_tenant: one per contract tenant, carried only in the issuer-signed grant (tenant_id)
identity.parent: every contract parent link is a signed parent reference (capability_id and content fingerprint); the provider answers with the complete chain
identity.request: fresh signed start request R′ per start attempt, with the lineage's fixed tool and arguments
identity.lineage: one per authority, created at setup through runtime calls only: process() of the authority's fixed ASK request (update_record); for initial issued also approve() with a signed human ApprovalGrantV3 and issuePermit(); confirmed in its initial state by the setup_baseline probe

approve.call: approve() with a signed human ApprovalGrantV3 built from the lineage snapshot

start.each_attempt: start({ lineage_id, request }) with a fresh signed request R′ under the authority's original capability

cases.tested_property: An authority revoked while its approval is pending: the approve, the issue and the start are denied, and nothing is approved, issued or started.
An approval granted before a capability revocation stays; the issue after the revocation and the start are denied, and nothing is issued or started.
A capability revoked while its lineage holds an issued, unused permit: the start and a fresh-ID retry start are both denied, and nothing starts.
A start before the permit is issued is denied (permit_not_issued); after the approval and the issue, a capability revocation covers the unused permit and a fresh-ID retry start is denied.
A capability revoked before its first start is denied at the start, although its lineage holds an issued, unused permit.
A repeated capability revocation is acknowledged (already_revoked) and still denies the start of a lineage with an issued, unused permit.
A session revocation denies the starts of two capabilities that share the revoked runtime session.
A session revocation fences the commit of a running execution; a running execution in another session of the same tenant still commits and delivers.
A commit before a session revocation stays; the delivery after it is withheld.
A tenant revocation fences the commits of running executions in two sessions of the tenant, and another tenant's execution in a session of the same name still commits and delivers.
A capability revocation fences the commit of an execution that started before it.
A capability revocation of a running execution: the cancellation is acknowledged, the commit is fenced and the delivery is withheld; the acknowledgement is not a terminal.

out_of_scope.reason: the tool function has already settled at finish; the runtime has no later delivery operation
commit of a/retry, an execution the runtime never started; there is no execution context to call

cases.tested_property: A commit before a capability revocation stays; the later delivery is withheld and a second commit is fenced.
A commit and a delivery before a capability revocation stay; the terminal follows at finish.
A commit observed at its own step before a capability revocation; cancellation acknowledged after the revocation.

out_of_scope.reason: the tool function has already settled at finish; the runtime has no later delivery operation

cases.tested_property: An ancestor revocation denies the start of an issued descendant and the approval and the issue of a pending descendant of that descendant.
A capability revocation of an ancestor fences the commit of a running execution of its issuer-attested descendant.

A capability revocation of a child (issuer-attested parent link to a) leaves its parent and its sibling (same parent, same runtime session) starting, committing and delivering: revocation never propagates upward or sideways.
A session revocation leaves another session of the same tenant usable.
A tenant revocation denies the start of the revoked tenant's authority and leaves another tenant's authority, in a session of the same name, starting, committing and delivering.

out_of_scope.reason: the denial rests on execution_id_in_use alone, which the runtime does not enforce
commit of b/e1, an execution the runtime never started; there is no execution context to call

cases.tested_property: The single-use permit: the first start runs, commits and delivers; a fresh-ID retry start against the consumed permit is denied (permit_consumed) and starts nothing.
A complete lifecycle before a capability revocation (approve, issue, start, commit, deliver, finish) stays; the revocation after the terminal changes nothing.
After a capability revocation and an acknowledged cancellation, the terminal follows at finish and a later commit through the retained context is fenced.
